questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of basic Swarm deployment, secret/config handling, and safe canary rollouts with health checks.

## Key Concepts
- Docker Secrets and Configs
- Overlay networks and Swarm deploy
- Canary rollouts and rollback on health failure
- Basic log-shipper sidecar

## Code Example
```yaml
version: '3.8'
services:
  api:
    image: myorg/api:latest
    secrets:
      - tls.crt
      - tls.key
    configs:
      - source: nginx_canary_conf
        target: /etc/nginx/conf.d/canary.conf
    deploy:
      replicas: 3
      update_config:
        parallelism: 1
        order: start-first
      health_check:
        test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -f https://localhost/health || exit 1"]
        interval: 10s
        timeout: 5s
        retries: 3
    networks:
      - overlay_net
  nginx:
    image: nginx:alpine
    secrets:
      - tls.crt
      - tls.key
    configs:
      - source: nginx_canary_conf
        target: /etc/nginx/conf.d/canary.conf
    deploy:
      replicas: 2
      update_config:
        parallelism: 1
        order: start-first
    networks:
      - overlay_net
  log-shipper:
    image: myorg/log-shipper:latest
    volumes:
      - logs:/var/log/app
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
    networks:
      - overlay_net
volumes:
  logs:
networks:
  overlay_net:
    driver: overlay
```

- How would you verify the 15% canary routing meets latency SLA?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests practical skills in observability, canary deployments, and Docker DCA cluster management.

## Key Concepts

- OpenTelemetry instrumentation and Jaeger trace visualization
- OTLP (OpenTelemetry Protocol) exporter configuration
- Nginx traffic splitting and header-based canary routing
- Prometheus metrics collection and TLS-secured API exposure
- Docker DCA cluster orchestration with docker-compose

## Code Example

```yaml
version: '3.8'
services:
  api-v1:
    image: myrepo/api:v1
    environment:
      - OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=api-v1
      - OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=otel-collector:4317
  
  api-v2:
    image: myrepo/api:v2
    environment:
      - OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=api-v2
      - OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=otel-collector:4317
  
  nginx:
    image: nginx:latest
    ports:
      - '443:443'
    volumes:
      - ./nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf:ro
      - ./certs:/etc/nginx/certs:ro
  
  otel-collector:
    image: otel/opentelemetry-collector:latest
    volumes:
      - ./otel-config.yaml:/etc/otel/config.yaml:ro
  
  jaeger:
    image: jaegertracing/all-in-one:1.42
    ports:
      - '16686:16686'
  
  prometheus:
    image: prom/prometheus:latest
    ports:
      - '9090:9090'
    volumes:
      - ./prometheus.yml:/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml:ro
```

```bash
# Deploy the cluster
docker-compose up -d

# Verify services
docker-compose ps

# Test canary routing

```

## Why This Is Asked

- docker-compose multi-service orchestration

# Dockerfile for API

COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm install
COPY . .
EXPOSE 3000
CMD node server.js

```yaml
# docker-compose.yml
version: '3.8'
services:
  api:
    build: ./api
    depends_on:
      - redis
    environment:
      - REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379
    healthcheck:
      test: curl -f http://localhost:3000/health || exit 1
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
    volumes:

  redis:

      - api
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Explores advanced isolation techniques using eBPF at the host level within multi-tenant Docker DCA environments, addressing practical security challenges in distributed systems.

## Key Concepts
- eBPF-based network security enforcement at the kernel level
- Tenant isolation through cgroups and user namespaces
- Edge TLS termination with Nginx reverse proxy
- Dynamic policy distribution via Vault for secrets management
- Centralized audit logging and observability with SIEM integration
- Canary deployment strategies for policy updates with fail-closed security posture

## Code Example

```bash
# Bootstrap commands
docker swarm init --advertise-addr <NODE1_IP>
docker network create --driver overlay --opt encrypted tenant-net

# Deploy eBPF policy daemon
docker service create --name policy-daemon \
  --mount type=bind,src=/sys/fs/cgroup,dst=/sys/fs/cgroup \
  --env VAULT_ADDR=https://vault.internal \
  policy-daemon:latest

# docker-compose.yml skeleton
version: '3.8'
services:
  nginx:
    image: nginx:alpine
    ports:
      - "443:443"
    volumes:
      - ./nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf
      - ./certs:/etc/nginx/certs
    deploy:
      replicas: 3
      placement:
        constraints:
          - node.role == worker

  api:
    image: myapp:latest
    networks:
      - tenant-net
    deploy:
      replicas: 2
      update_config:
        parallelism: 1
        delay: 10s
        order: start-first
        failure_action: rollback
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you validate tenant A vs tenant B network isolation in production?
- What strategies would you use for zero-downtime eBPF program updates?
- How would you handle policy rollback if canary deployment detects issues?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical mTLS implementation, Docker secrets management, and edge proxy configuration in a Swarm environment. Evaluates operational skills for secure service-to-service communication.

## Key Concepts
- Docker secrets for TLS certificate management
- Nginx mutual TLS verification and client certificate validation
- Client identity propagation to backend services via HTTP headers

## Code Example
```yaml
# skeleton docker-compose.yml
version: '3.9'
services:
  edge:
    image: nginx:alpine
    ports:
      - '443:443'
    secrets:
      - source: nginx_server_cert
        target: server.crt
      - source: nginx_server_key
        target: server.key
      - source: nginx_ca_cert
        target: ca.pem
    configs:
      - source: nginx_config
        target: /etc/nginx/nginx.conf
  api:
    image: your-api:latest
    deploy:
      replicas: 2
secrets:
  nginx_server_cert:
    external: true
  nginx_server_key:
    external: true
  nginx_ca_cert:
    external: true
configs:
  nginx_config:
    external: true
```

## Certificate Generation
```bash
# Create private CA
openssl genrsa -out ca.key 4096
openssl req -new -x509 -days 365 -key ca.key -out ca.pem

# Generate server certificate
openssl genrsa -out server.key 2048
openssl req -new -key server.key -out server.csr
openssl x509 -req -in server.csr -CA ca.pem -CAkey ca.key -CAcreateserial -out server.crt -days 365

# Generate client certificate
openssl genrsa -out client.key 2048
openssl req -new -key client.key -out client.csr
openssl x509 -req -in client.csr -CA ca.pem -CAkey ca.key -CAcreateserial -out client.crt -days 365

# Create Docker secrets
docker secret create nginx_server_cert server.crt
docker secret create nginx_server_key server.key
docker secret create nginx_ca_cert ca.pem
```

## Testing Commands
```bash
# Test with client certificate
curl --cert client.crt --key client.key --cacert ca.pem https://your-service:443/api

# Test without client certificate (should fail)
curl --cacert ca.pem https://your-service:443/api

# Verify client identity header
curl --cert client.crt --key client.key --cacert ca.pem https://your-service:443/api -v | grep X-Client-Subject
```
